title: The Swallow and the Crow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Swallow was once boasting to a Crow about her birth. "I was once a princess," said she, "the daughter of a King of Athens, but my husband used me cruelly, and cut out my tongue for a slight fault. Then, to protect me from further injury, I was turned by Juno into a bird." "You chatter quite enough as it is," said the Crow. "What you would have been like if you hadn't lost your tongue, I can't think."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Swallow boasting to the Crow about?
According to the passage, what does the Swallow claim she once was?
options: A princess, daughter of a King of Athens

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Swallow say happened to her tongue?
options: She lost it in a hunting accident
Her husband cut it out for a slight fault
It was stolen by a rival princess

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who turned the Swallow into a bird?
As the passage uses it, what does "boasting" mean in "boasting to a Crow about her birth"?
As the passage uses it, what does "chatter" mean in "You chatter quite enough as it is"?
Based on the passage, why is the Crow's remark about the Swallow's tongue a witty put-down?
options: It proves the Swallow's story about Juno is false
It shows the Crow also lost a body part once
It suggests the Swallow talks constantly even now, so having her tongue would have made her unbearable
It reveals the Crow cannot understand the Swallow's speech

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Birds should never discuss their family history
Claims of past grandeur do not impress others, especially when undercut by one's own present behavior
Juno is unkind to mistreated princesses
Crows are always more honest than swallows

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Swallow say her husband cut out her tongue?
options: Because she refused to marry him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why was the Swallow turned into a bird?
options: To help her escape from Athens
To protect her from further injury

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "cruelly" mean in "my husband used me cruelly"?
As the passage uses it, what does "injury" mean in "protect me from further injury"?
Based on the passage, what does calling her fault "slight" suggest about the Swallow's view of her husband's punishment?
options: She believes the punishment was fair and well-deserved
She sees the punishment as extreme compared to how minor the offense was
She thinks she deserved an even harsher punishment
She has forgotten what the fault actually was

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Crow tells a Swallow a sad story about her own life
A Swallow and a Crow compete over who sings better
A Crow apologizes to a Swallow for a past wrong
A Swallow boasts to a Crow about once being a mistreated princess, and the Crow mocks her by noting how talkative she still is
